correctness.rationale: The beta-binomial stationary M-block is invariant by beta predictive consistency; the finite shift-register chain is irreducible and aperiodic. Initial short-lag covariance is exactly v/(kappa+1), the longer lags obey the stated linear recurrence, and summing the absolutely convergent covariance series gives (M+kappa)(M+kappa+1)/(kappa(kappa+1)). The standard finite-state functional CLT and discrete integration by parts give Gaussian edge fluctuations; a covariance-sum dominated-convergence argument proves variance convergence independently. The infinite-memory contrast follows from beta de Finetti and strong laws. Exact finite-state Poisson-equation and exhaustive graph checks passed in verify.py. Fixed-M scope and connected last-vertex perturbation are explicitly justified.

value.rationale: The source explicitly motivates stochastic analysis of its finite-memory graph model. The exact polynomial all-memory variance coefficient quantifies the nontrivial quadratic inflation caused by longer window dependence, resolves the weighted edge-count Gaussian fluctuation scale and sharply contrasts finite-memory deterministic edge density with infinite-memory random edge density. It is a natural global graph invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice, and covers every fixed positive integer memory length and all positive urn parameters.
